title: Crispy Cornmeal Shrimp Po' Boys with Creole Mayo
summary: Prawns are coated in seasoned flour, egg and a Creole cornmeal mix, chilled, deep-fried until golden and opaque, then piled into rolls with Creole mayo, lettuce, tomato and pickles.
equipment: wire rack set on a baking tray

ingredients.item: raw peeled and deveined large prawns
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
crusty sub rolls or 20 cm lengths of soft baguette

steps.title: Make the seasoning and mayo
steps.text: Mix all the Creole seasoning in a small dish. Whisk 1 tsp of it into the mayonnaise with the hot sauce and lemon juice, then chill.

steps.title: Set up the coating
steps.text: Put half the flour and half the remaining seasoning in one dish, the beaten eggs in a second, and the rest of the flour and seasoning mixed with the cornmeal in a third.

steps.title: Coat the prawns
steps.text: Pat the prawns dry. Coat each in flour, dip in egg and press into the cornmeal mix. Set on the rack and chill for 15 minutes so the coating sets.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil to 180 °C in the saucepan, no more than one-third full. Fry the prawns in 3 batches for 2-3 minutes until deep golden, curled and opaque right through (63 °C). Drain on kitchen paper and let the oil return to 180 °C between batches.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Split the rolls and spread both sides with Creole mayo. Layer on lettuce, tomato, pickles and the hot prawns and serve straight away.

tips: Chilling the coated prawns stops the coating falling off in the oil.
Don't crowd the pan; too many prawns at once drop the oil temperature and make them greasy.
Never leave hot oil unattended, and keep a lid nearby.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten immediately; fried prawns lose their crunch quickly. Refrigerate any leftover prawns within 1 hour and use within 1 day. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
